title: 2008 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: A class collects \(\$50\) to buy flowers for a classmate who is in the hospital. Roses cost \(\$3\) each, and carnations cost \(\$2\) each. No other flowers are to be used. How many different bouquets could be purchased for exactly \(\$50?\)

solutions.text:
If \(r\) roses and \(c\) carnations are bought, then \(3r+2c=50.\) Because \(2c\) and \(50\) are even, \(3r\) must be even, so \(r\) is even.

Also \(3r\le 50,\) so \(r\le 16.\) The even values \(r=0,2,4,\ldots,16\) each give a valid \(c,\) which is \(9\) bouquets.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(r\) be the number of roses; then \(3r+2c=50\)
Since \(2c\) is even and \(50\) is even, \(r\) must be even, and \(3r\le 50\)
